artworks.title: Nymphs Finding the Head of Orpheus
artworks.description: Waterhouse paints the aftermath of the Thracian sparagmos: two nymphs lean over a woodland pool where Orpheus' severed head still rests upon his lyre. Pre-Raphaelite stillness turns the myth's most violent end into a quiet, haunted discovery.

artworks.title: Orpheus
artworks.description: A Thracian girl cradles Orpheus' severed head where it has come to rest on his own lyre, head and instrument fused into a single relic. Moreau turns the myth's most violent moment into still, jewelled mourning; the painting entered the French state collections in his lifetime and now hangs in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

artworks.title: The Death of Orpheus
artworks.description: Dürer's Hamburg drawing — Thracian women killing the bard who refused their love after Eurydice, Northern Renaissance violence for Apollodorus' and Ovid's Maenad murder.

films.title: Black Orpheus
films.description: Camus' Carnival Orpheus ends torn by jealous Bacchantes — the Thracian death replayed under Rio's sun.

popCulture.title: Orpheus
popCulture.description: The head that still sings after the Maenads — Orpheus' death remains the poet's martyrdom in Western art.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 11 — the Ciconian women drown Orpheus' song with drums, then tear him; Bacchus roots the killers into oaks.
